title.narrative: Enhancing Entrepreneurial Capacities within Agri‑Food Value Chains in Ouagadougou
Rafforzamento imprenditoriale delle filiere agroalimentari a Ouagadougou - RAGOUA

description.narrative: L’iniziativa promuove lo sviluppo economico sostenibile e inclusivo a Ouagadougou e nella Grand Ouaga attraverso il rafforzamento delle filiere agroalimentari urbane e periurbane, con particolare attenzione a giovani, donne, persone con disabilità, sfollati interni e gruppi in condizione di vulnerabilità. L’intervento intende migliorare la competitività delle micro, piccole e medie imprese attive nella produzione, trasformazione e commercializzazione di alimenti freschi e trasformati, favorendo occupazione dignitosa, imprenditorialità, resilienza ai rischi e pratiche di consumo responsabile. Le attività si articolano in tre componenti integrate. La prima componente rafforza le competenze tecnico‑gestionali delle imprese locali attraverso percorsi di formazione, coaching personalizzato, educazione finanziaria, strumenti digitali di marketing e l’introduzione di pratiche agroecologiche che promuovono la rigenerazione del suolo, la gestione sostenibile dell’acqua e la riduzione degli input chimici. Il percorso formativo è progettato per incrementare l’autonomia economica di donne, giovani e persone vulnerabili, riducendo le barriere all’inclusione nelle filiere. La seconda componente sostiene l’innovazione imprenditoriale tramite programmi strutturati di incubazione e pre‑incubazione. Le imprese selezionate beneficeranno di mentoring, supporto tecnico specializzato, spazi di coworking e laboratori attivati da precedenti iniziative, oltre a meccanismi finanziari finalizzati a facilitare investimenti iniziali, crescita aziendale e accesso al credito. La terza componente interviene sui mercati urbani e sulle strutture di vendita decentrate, migliorandone infrastrutture, logistica, standard igienico‑sanitari e condizioni operative. Sono previste diagnosi partecipative, interventi strutturali leggeri, formazione su igiene e gestione dei rifiuti, uso di checklist ispirate agli standard internazionali in materia di sicurezza alimentare e azioni per rafforzare la governance locale dei mercati, rendendoli più sicuri, accessibili e attrattivi per venditori e consumatori. Beneficiari diretti dell’iniziativa saranno micro, piccole e medie imprese, cooperative, produttori agroecologici, trasformatori, venditori dei mercati urbani e periurbani, donne imprenditrici, giovani e persone vulnerabili, incluse persone con disabilità e sfollati interni. Beneficiari indiretti saranno le comunità dell’area metropolitana, che potranno contare su un sistema alimentare più efficiente, prodotti di migliore qualità e mercati meglio organizzati. L’iniziativa contribuisce agli Obiettivi di Sviluppo Sostenibile relativi a sicurezza alimentare, parità di genere, lavoro dignitoso, rafforzamento delle economie locali, modelli sostenibili di produzione e consumo e adattamento ai cambiamenti climatici. La rilevanza strategica deriva dalla piena coerenza con le priorità nazionali burkinabé, con il quadro programmatorio della Cooperazione Italiana e con le iniziative Team Europa incentrate su sistemi alimentari sostenibili, occupazione giovanile, transizione verde e rafforzamento delle filiere locali.

The initiative promotes sustainable and inclusive economic development in the urban and peri urban areas of Ouagadougou and the Grand Ouaga by strengthening local agri food value chains, with a particular focus on young people, women, persons with disabilities, internally displaced people and other vulnerable groups. Its objective is to enhance the competitiveness of micro, small and medium enterprises engaged in food production, processing and marketing, while fostering decent employment, entrepreneurship, resilience and responsible consumption practices. The intervention is structured around three complementary components. The first component focuses on building the technical and managerial capacities of local enterprises through training programmes, personalised coaching, financial education, digital marketing tools and the introduction of agroecological practices aimed at soil regeneration, sustainable water management and reduced use of chemical inputs, with a strong emphasis on the economic empowerment of women and youth. The second component supports innovation and enterprise development through structured incubation and pre incubation pathways. Selected businesses receive mentoring, specialised technical assistance, access to co working and processing spaces established through previous initiatives, and tailored financial mechanisms to facilitate initial investments and business consolidation, promoting youth entrepreneurship and sustainable economic inclusion. The third component aims to improve the organisation, infrastructure and hygiene standards of urban markets and decentralised selling points through baseline assessments, light infrastructure upgrades, training on hygiene and waste management, the use of checklists aligned with international food safety standards and measures to strengthen local market governance, making markets safer, more accessible and more attractive for vendors and consumers. Direct beneficiaries include micro, small and medium enterprises, cooperatives, agroecological producers, processors, market vendors, women entrepreneurs, young people and vulnerable individuals, including persons with disabilities and internally displaced people. Indirect beneficiaries are the broader communities of Ouagadougou and the municipalities of the Greater Ouaga, who will benefit from improved food availability, better product quality and more dynamic local markets. The initiative contributes to Sustainable Development Goals related to food security, economic inclusion, gender equality, decent work, sustainable consumption and production and climate resilience, and is strategically aligned with national priorities of Burkina Faso, the programming framework of the Italian Cooperation and relevant Team Europe Initiatives.

tag.narrative: By 2020, substantially reduce the proportion of youth not in employment, education or training
By 2030, achieve full and productive employment and decent work for all women and men, including for young people and persons with disabilities, and equal pay for work of equal value

By 2030, double the agricultural productivity and incomes of small-scale food producers, in particular women, indigenous peoples, family farmers, pastoralists and fishers, including through secure and equal access to land, other productive resources and inputs, knowledge, financial services, markets and opportunities for value addition and non-farm employment
By 2030, enhance inclusive and sustainable urbanization and capacity for participatory, integrated and sustainable human settlement planning and management in all countries

By 2030, ensure sustainable food production systems and implement resilient agricultural practices that increase productivity and production, that help maintain ecosystems, that strengthen capacity for adaptation to climate change, extreme weather, drought, flooding and other disasters and that progressively improve land and soil quality
By 2030, halve per capita global food waste at the retail and consumer levels and reduce food losses along production and supply chains, including post-harvest losses
By 2030, substantially reduce waste generation through prevention, reduction, recycling and reuse
End hunger, achieve food security and improved nutrition and promote sustainable agriculture
Ensure sustainable consumption and production patterns
Make cities and human settlements inclusive, safe, resilient and sustainable

Promote development-oriented policies that support productive activities, decent job creation, entrepreneurship, creativity and innovation, and encourage the formalization and growth of micro-, small- and medium-sized enterprises, including through access to financial services
Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all
Strengthen resilience and adaptive capacity to climate-related hazards and natural disasters in all countries
Support positive economic, social and environmental links between urban, peri-urban and rural areas by strengthening national and regional development planning
Take urgent action to combat climate change and its impacts
